current_determination: R61 fixes the endpoint normalization type. A terminal dimensionless coupling is insufficient: the renormalization datum is (scheme, mu_*, g_*), or equivalently a scheme-dependent Lambda parameter once the beta flow is known. In a constant inverse-square-drift model Lambda_disc = mu exp[-(log L/b) g^{-2}] is exactly invariant, making the R60 N^{-1/2} bare-coupling law equivalent to dimensional transmutation. Abstractly, if the native inverse-square beta increments are positive, uniformly bounded and the one-step maps are invertible, then every weak endpoint admits a unique depth-N backward-tuned scalar trajectory with the entire trajectory remaining in the weak collar. This scalar theorem is a derivation, not a source-attested CMP109 theorem until the exact Paper-I inequalities are extracted. More importantly, equal endpoint coupling across cutoff depths does not imply convergence of the full endpoint effective density: irrelevant/localized coordinates may retain N-dependence. EndpointDensityConvergence is therefore the next cross-cutoff continuum-construction obligation. Endpoint normalization/Lambda selection does not prove mass generation and remains separate from the later UV-to-IR massive-basin handoff.
major_new_results: Renormalization endpoint typed as (scheme, mu_*, g_*), not g_* alone.
Endpoint scale-coupling condition and scheme-dependent Lambda are alternative labels of the same RG trajectory once the beta flow is known.
Constant inverse-square drift gives the discrete invariant Lambda_disc = mu exp[-(log L/b) g^{-2}].
Positive bounded invertible beta corridor implies unique backward scalar tuning to a fixed weak endpoint for every finite UV depth.
Backward tuning yields x_*+N b_- <= x_0^(N) <= x_*+N b_+ and therefore g_0^(N) ~ N^{-1/2} while every intermediate coupling remains <= g_*.
Fixing the endpoint marginal coordinate across N does not force equality or convergence of irrelevant/localized endpoint-density coordinates.
EndpointDensityConvergence is identified as the next cross-cutoff obligation.
